I will do it the way I usually do here, starting from what worked for me last year and what I saw on the nearby fields. I have 10.9 mu total, so I will keep part in cotton and the rest in the wheat-maize rotation. Cotton takes more watching, but if I feed it well and keep the worms down, it still gives me cash. Wheat and maize are my steady crops, and with well water I do not want to let them go hungry. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. I do not make big risky changes. If a seed did well for people around me, I will use that kind again. For tillage, I will keep it simple: rotary tillage for wheat and maize land because it is faster and cheaper, and plough the cotton land once so the soil is looser. On fertilizer, I will put enough base fertilizer first, then topdress nitrogen when the crop starts pushing hard. On water, wheat gets more because spring wind here dries the land fast, maize gets a couple of good irrigations if rain is short, and cotton gets fewer but timed at the important stages. On pesticide, I will spray when I see the problem starting, but for cotton I will spray more times because that crop is easy to lose if I wait too long.
